title: Root-Zone Water Content, Dryback, Runoff & Crop Steering
level: Environmental, Irrigation & Fertigation Systems Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Cultivation personnel responsible for root-zone moisture interpretation, irrigation-response analysis, runoff/return trending and advanced crop-steering support
prerequisites: Irrigation Design, Flow, Pressure, Uniformity & Maintenance or equivalent advanced irrigation foundation
evidencePolicy: Course uses controlled irrigation, root-zone nutrient and cannabis soilless-media evidence. Dryback and crop-steering concepts are taught as measured trajectories and response frameworks; no single dryback percentage, runoff fraction, irrigation interval, feed EC or steering recipe is presented as a universal cannabis target.
assessmentPolicy: Development-only until technical/assessment review, accessibility review and pilot evidence are complete. Course completion does not authorize unreviewed crop-steering strategies, nutrient-formulation redesign or production setpoint changes outside assigned authority.
description: Develops specialist interpretation of root-zone water content, dryback trajectories, runoff/return evidence, EC concentration, substrate/media behavior and measured crop-steering decisions.
learningOutcomes: Interpret root-zone water content as a spatial and temporal state influenced by substrate/media properties, container geometry, root development, irrigation delivery and environmental demand.
Calculate and analyze dryback as a trajectory between verified measurements rather than treating elapsed time or one percentage as a universal target.
Use runoff or return volume and chemistry together with input, root-zone and delivery evidence to distinguish drainage, preferential flow, concentration and sampling effects.
Evaluate crop-steering adjustments from measured root-zone, environment and crop response while preserving study/system boundaries and avoiding universal recipes.
Produce a reconstructable root-zone steering report that states baseline, intervention, measured response, uncertainty, acceptance limits and authorized next action.
